newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee cuts losses by noon.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee cuts losses by noon.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures ended Monday midsession with pared losses after an earlier wave of Far East origin selling and sell-stops ebbed, traders said.
Support to the market came mostly from light jobber activity.
By the midday pause, September finished just $20 down at $1,755 a tonne after gapping $10 up at $1,785, the day's peak, the start.
The market was earlier called $30 higher after a firm close on New York on Friday.
But values soon headed south and light sell-stops emerged after September triggered $1,755 on the way down. It hit a floor at $1,744 before jobber buying re-appeared.
Volume was small at 1,971 lots, again centred on September contract.
Coffee's dull, rangebound trade continued to highlight lack of fresh fundamental inputs. Brazilian winter remained mild while certified stocks in New York continued to build up.
The U.S. June green coffee stocks due after the close of New York trading on Tuesday were expected to show a fall or an increase of 100,000 bags.
LIFFE June cerfitied stock data are also due at lunchtime in London on Tuesday.
Chartwise, the market showed little sign of the direction of the next move.
The only way to tell the direction of coffee's next big move was to see wether support or resistance went first and "follow the break", Adrian Haylor, technical analyst at Sucden, said.
